title: Small and real
hook: a practice you keep beats a perfect one you don't; the widow's two mites outweigh the rich gifts (Mark 12:41-44)
tomorrow: one went home and one stayed. which daughter-in-law was right?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: one gap. The four sights showed Siddhartha what his palace left out. Once you find a gap, the temptation is to fill it all at once.

Two gifts reach the school fundraiser in the same week: a big check from a company, and an envelope from a grandmother on a fixed income with a ten-dollar bill folded inside. On paper, one is far larger. The Gospel of Mark has a scene about exactly that arithmetic. Jesus sits across from the temple treasury in Jerusalem, watching people drop in their offerings. Rich people come by and cast in much. Then a poor widow comes, and she throws in two mites, two tiny coins. Jesus calls his disciples over. He wants them to see this one.
screen: `A BIG CHECK, A FOLDED TEN.` → `JESUS WATCHES THE TREASURY.` → `THE RICH CAST IN MUCH.` → `A WIDOW: TWO MITES.`

segments.voice: "Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury." More? Two tiny coins? Jesus explains: they gave out of their abundance, "but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living." Their gifts were big, and cost them nothing they'd miss. Hers was small, and it was real. Here's the teaching Christians take from it. In Jesus' accounting, a gift is weighed by what it costs the giver, not by the number on it. Now carry that to practice. A grand plan written on a Sunday night is like the rich men's offerings: it looks large, and it hasn't cost anything yet. A practice you'll actually keep, five minutes, one Saturday, one call, is the widow's coins. Notice what Jesus does not say. He doesn't tell the rich to stop giving, and he doesn't praise small for being small. He praises real: the gift that's actually given, from what she actually had. So the question for any plan isn't, is it big enough? It's, is it real? Will you put it in, this week, with what you've got? Small and real beats large and imagined.
screen: `MORE THAN ALL OF THEM.` · `THEIR ABUNDANCE, HER WANT.` · `WEIGHED BY WHAT IT COST HER.` · `NOT SMALL FOR ITS OWN SAKE: REAL.` · then, large: `SMALL AND REAL.`

segments.voice: Take one plan you've made in this new stretch and shrink it until it fits your real week. Then do its smallest piece now: one line read, one glass of water for a plant, one slow minute of quiet.
Small and real: a practice you'll actually keep, like the widow's two mites, which Jesus said were more than all the rich men's gifts.
Your line: small and real. Two coins, given whole, outweighed all the rest. That's day 1594.

howItsDone: Christians read the widow's offering in Mark 12 as a teaching on giving from the heart, measured by what it costs the giver, not by its size.

fork.setup: your friend wants to start praying, but she's embarrassed: she can manage five minutes, and her aunt prays for an hour. what fits the widow's mites?
options: five minutes really given count; the widow's coins weren't measured against the rich.
wait until she can manage the hour; anything smaller doesn't count.
give up; if she can't match her aunt, it's better not to try.
fork.reveal: Jesus didn't rank the widow below the rich for giving less; he said she gave more, because it was really given, from what she had.

original.note: Greek: lepta, small coins; the 'two mites' the widow gives in Mark 12:42.

trapdoor: what you thought: a serious practice has to be big and impressive.

what a scholar hears: Mark 12:41-44, two lepta that 'make a farthing', given 'of her want', set against the abundance of the rich.
guess: a practice small enough to really keep, given wholeheartedly

a cheap version you do until you can afford the real one

chat.meaning: Jesus said the widow's two mites were more than the rich gifts, because she really gave from what she had. Small and real counts.

tie.story: the rich cast in much from their abundance; the widow cast in two mites, all she had, and Jesus said she gave more.
tie.friend: Zoe can trade three imagined nights at the garden nursery for one Saturday morning she'll really show up for.
